ChecksumContent.title: ChecksumContent

CitationModel.description:
BibTeX model for citations.

https://www.bibtex.com/format/

Includes some non-standard fields.

author.description: The name(s) of the author(s) (in the case of more than one author, separated by `and`).
author.title: Author

url.description: The URL field is used to store the URL of a web page or FTP download. It is a non-standard BibTeX field.
url.title: Url

institution.description: The institution that was involved in the publishing, but not necessarily the publisher.
institution.title: Institution

doi.description: The doi field is used to store the digital object identifier (DOI) of a journal article, conference paper, book chapter or book. It is a non-standard BibTeX field. It's recommended to simply use the DOI, and not a DOI link.
doi.title: Doi

month.description: The month of publication (or, if unpublished, the month of creation). Use three-letter abbreviation.
month.title: Month

year.description: The year of publication (or, if unpublished, the year of creation).
year.title: Year

licence.description: The terms under which the associated resource are licenced for reuse.
licence.title: Licence

CitationModel.title: CitationModel

ColumnModel.description: A data source's column, by its name as the source writes it, typed in whyqd's types only.

uuid.description: Unique identity for the column. Automatically generated.
uuid.title: Uuid

name.description: Column label / name from source data. In whatever format it was written, including leading/lagging spaces, non-printing characters, etc.
name.title: Name

type.description: A column must contain values of a specific type. Default is 'string'.

profile.description: What the column holds, as read, in counts.

ColumnModel.title: ColumnModel

DialectModel.description:
How a file is written, so it can be read: the dialect of the W3C's CSV on the Web metadata vocabulary
([Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data, section 5.9](https://www.w3.org/TR/tabular-metadata/#dialect-descriptions)),
with its names and defaults, and whyqd's own: `encodingStep`, `rowsPerRecord`, `sheet`, and, for a PDF, `cells`,
`pages`, and `columns`.

One default differs: CSV on the Web trims each cell, and whyqd keeps it as written (`trim` false). A blank line is
a row (`skipBlankRows` false), in both.

encoding.description: The file's encoding, as the WHATWG Encoding Standard names it.
encoding.title: Encoding

quoteChar.description: The character quoting a cell; `null` for none.
quoteChar.title: Quotechar

doubleQuote.description: A quote inside a quoted cell is doubled; if false, escaped by `\`.
doubleQuote.title: Doublequote

skipRows.description: Rows before the header, or before the data where there is no header.
skipRows.title: Skiprows

headerRowCount.description: Header rows; `0` where the file has none.
headerRowCount.title: Headerrowcount

skipBlankRows.description: Leave out blank rows. By default a blank row is a row.
skipBlankRows.title: Skipblankrows

rowsPerRecord.description: The fields in each row of one record, header included, where a record spans several rows: `[47, 1]` is 47 fields on the first row and 1 on the next. Absent where a record is one row.
rowsPerRecord.title: Rowsperrecord

sheet.description: The spreadsheet's sheet, where the file has several.
sheet.title: Sheet

cells.description: How a PDF's cells are found: by its ruling (`lines`), or by where its text sits (`text`). Read from the file where undeclared: `lines` where its ruling gives a table, else `text`.
cells.title: Cells

pages.description: A PDF's pages holding the table, counted from 1: `5-7`, or `1,3,5-7`. Absent for every page.
pages.title: Pages

columns.description: The left edge of each of a PDF table's columns, in points from the page's left, where its cells are found by `text` and the words do not show the columns.
columns.title: Columns

DialectModel.title: DialectModel

ProfileModel.description: What a column holds, as read, in counts. Profiling never changes a cell.

cellTypes.description: Cells of each type, as the reader found them.
cellTypes.title: Celltypes

dateLike.description: Text cells that look like a date.
dateLike.title: Datelike

zeroPadded.description: Text cells holding a number with leading zeros.
zeroPadded.title: Zeropadded

numberFormats.description: Number and date cells by the format code an `.xlsx` stores for them; empty for other files.
numberFormats.title: Numberformats

uuid.description: Automatically generated unique identity for the data source.
uuid.title: Uuid

title.description: A descriptive name for the data source.
title.title: Title

description.description: A complete description of the data source. Depending on how complex your work becomes, try and be as helpful as possible to 'future-you'. You'll thank yourself later.
description.title: Description

path.description: Full path to valid source data file.
path.title: Path

mime.description: Mime type for source data. Automatically generated.

header.description: Row (0-indexed) to use for the column labels of the parsed DataFrame.
header.title: Header

sheet_name.description: Needed if MimeType is either of XLS or XLSX, and the data consists of multiple sheets.
sheet_name.title: Sheet Name

names.description: If the source data has no header row, explicitly pass a list of column names - in the correct order - to address the data. May not be known until after initial wrangling.
names.title: Names

columns.description: List of ColumnModel with names & type derived from the source data. In table order.
columns.title: Columns

preserve.description: List of columns where variable type guessing must be prevented and the original data preserved. Critical for foreign key references with weird formats, like integers with leading `0`.
preserve.title: Preserve

key.description: A list of key columns required before merging of multiple data sources into an interim data source.
key.title: Key

dialect.description: How the file is written, so it can be read.

hidden.description: The publisher hid this sheet of the workbook; it is read like any other. Absent where visible.
hidden.title: Hidden

attributes.description: Optional open dictionary for reader-specific attributes for Pandas' API. E.g. 'quoting' for the CSV library.

checksums.description: Checksums proving the source data, each naming what it hashed: the table as 1.x read it, or the file's bytes.
checksums.title: Checksums

index.description: Count of rows in source data table.
index.title: Index

citation.description: Optional full citation for the source data.
